title: Floor tile setting
use_case: Floor tiling: a 300 x 300 mm porcelain floor tile (10 mm thick, 2.2 kg) goes on the fresh adhesive bed, where it sits about 2 mm proud of its finished height until it is pressed. Lay it on the bed, then tamp it down level: within 1 mm of its finished height and no more than 0.5 degrees out of level, pressing no harder than 60 N.
headline: A two-tool head completes the task in 8 of 8 runs.

plan.title: Floor tiling
plan.description: Lift a 300x300 mm porcelain tile and set it on the fresh adhesive bed, then press it down until it is within 1 mm of its finished height and no more than 0.5 degrees out of level, using no more than 60 N of pressing force.
assumptions: Adhesive bed yields at 30 N and hardens 15 N/mm; pressing ~28 N sinks the tile ~1.3 mm to meet height tolerance after spring‑back.

steps.description: Lift the tile and set it back on the adhesive bed.
caveats: The mortar bed is an approximation: nine plastic cells that yield and harden linearly and keep their set; no flow, suction or curing. A screen, not a promise.

success.text: height err mm at most 1 mm

candidates.caveat: Vacuum area frame (approximation): the cups of the suction cup model on a rigid frame, each with its own seal test and its own vacuum valve (a cup that does not seal stays off). The holding force is the sum of the sealed cups' caps; the payload is that force over a safety factor (1.5 smooth, 2.0 porous, 2.5 swivelling, all [assumed]) at 1 g. Only the smooth rating is a simulated claim: the porous and swivelling ratings are arithmetic on the same force, because no leak, porosity or swivel is simulated. Not modelled: a shared vacuum source and its flow, the leak of an unsealed cup into the others, the frame's flex, peel across a long face, foam or needle area grippers. Treat frame results as a screen, then verify on hardware.

tool_details.display_name: Vacuum area frame, 2 x 2 cups, 300 mm
tool_details.rating: rated 4.15 kg on a smooth face (holding force over a 1.5 safety factor)
tool_details.caveat: Vacuum area frame (approximation): the cups of the suction cup model on a rigid frame, each with its own seal test and its own vacuum valve (a cup that does not seal stays off). The holding force is the sum of the sealed cups' caps; the payload is that force over a safety factor (1.5 smooth, 2.0 porous, 2.5 swivelling, all [assumed]) at 1 g. Only the smooth rating is a simulated claim: the porous and swivelling ratings are arithmetic on the same force, because no leak, porosity or swivel is simulated. Not modelled: a shared vacuum source and its flow, the leak of an unsealed cup into the others, the frame's flex, peel across a long face, foam or needle area grippers. Treat frame results as a screen, then verify on hardware.

tool_details.rating: rated 40 N (the stage slips at 60 N)
tool_details.caveat: Tamper pad (approximation): a rigid, level 200 mm square pad on a spring stage that slips at 60 N, so the pad never presses harder than that within the stage's 60 mm of travel. Not modelled: pad deformation, vibration or impact compaction, mortar flow, the pad's edge catching a joint. Simulated, verify on hardware.

finalists.label: Tool change: Suction cup > Tamper pad

tool_details.caveat: Suction cup (approximation): a compliant lip of rigid segments on a bellows spring with a limited tilt; the seal is a geometric test (every lip segment touching the face, part material under 13 rays inside the lip) gating a MuJoCo adhesion actuator capped at vacuum x lip area (at most 60 kPa). The lip must touch the face: no pull across a gap. Not modelled: air flow, leak rate, porosity, vacuum build-up time (the vacuum follows the shared close ramp and is cut the control tick the seal is lost), lip material hysteresis, peel dynamics beyond the contact distribution. The lip's friction is the part's. Treat suction results as a screen, then verify on hardware.
